_doc: The box-side facts that have NO source in this repo, and nothing else.
Everything derivable is derived by deploy/make_invariants.py from `git ls-files`, so this
file holds only the two things a repo cannot know: WHERE the daemon loads each artifact
from, and WHICH units must be alive. Adding a file here is almost always wrong; adding a
file to git is what should make it appear in the manifest.
Every path below is relative to ZEROCLAW_HOME (~/.zeroclaw), which is the root
deploy/box_selfcheck.py resolves against. That is deliberate and it is the whole point of
the `dst` field: on 2026-08-06 a rebuilt plugin was written to ~/zc-shop/plugins/ while the
daemon kept loading ~/.zeroclaw/plugins/, so the fresh artifact and the running one were
different files and every content hash in the world would have compared the wrong one.
A `dst` that is WRONG fails LOUD rather than silent: check_manifest reports the path it
looked for as MISSING. That is the safe direction, and it means a first run on the box is
how this file gets confirmed. The generator prints a reconcile command for exactly that.

map.why: The shared skill tree the agent loads. SKILL.md here is the worked example the model copies verbatim, which is how a stale mint and a devnet sentence reached a customer on 2026-08-06.

The jailed workspace copy the skill actually shells out to, once per order. It is a SECOND copy of the same file at a different path, and neither is tracked against the other, so a fix applied to one leaves the other live. Scoped to pay_link.py because that is the only member evidenced as deployed here; widening it is one edit once a box listing confirms the rest.
The agent workspace copy. SOPs also live in two places, and the evening-reconciliation read path stayed open for two hours after the skill write path was closed because only one copy was corrected.

The deterministic settlement announcer, and the literal ExecStart target of zc-announce.service (`%h/.zeroclaw/bin/announce_settlements.sh`). It exists to REPLACE the prose SOP whose reporting step let a model compose settlement fields: on 2026-08-06 that produced four fabricated ledger rows, two with a literal ellipsis where an 88-char signature belongs and two sharing one signature across different orders and amounts, none of which matched any of the merchant ATA's twelve lifetime signatures. The unit was written and this file never carried the script, so the deployer could not place it and the checker could not miss it, and a unit whose ExecStart does not exist fails 203/EXEC every tick while the prose path stays the only thing that would run. That is the whole defect class this map exists to close, landing on the one path that touches money.

THE CHECKER ITSELF, and the literal ExecStart target of zc-selfcheck.service (`%h/.zeroclaw/bin/box_selfcheck.py`). It was absent from this map until 2026-08-16, which made it the one file on the box that could drift with nothing able to report it: the deployer does not copy what the map does not list, and the manifest check cannot compare a file that is not in `files`, so the drift detector was the single artifact exempt from drift detection. Adding it here closes both halves at once -- sync_workspace places it, and its hash lands in the manifest, so a stale checker running against a fresh manifest now reports ITSELF as differing. Measured at the time: the live box served a verdict whose mint-prohibition wording (`unexpected address` for a state target, and a detail line with no finding count) belongs to a box_selfcheck that predates the denylist rewrite, while every one of the 19 files it compared reported match. The checker was four commits stale and its own output was the only evidence. THE MIRROR CASE IS MEASURED AND IT MEANS THIS ENTRY CANNOT SHIP ALONE. A FRESH checker against a STALE manifest reports itself as differing just as loudly as the stale-checker case above, because the pin is on CONTENT and the comparison is symmetric. Installing only this file on a box whose SHOP-INVARIANTS.json was generated at an older commit turns `manifest` red with `bin/box_selfcheck.py: <new> != <old>`, the oneshot unit exits 1 because a DRIFTED verdict is a non-zero exit, and the gate then publishes ok:false on the public /selfcheck route. Measured 2026-08-20 against DEPLOYED_SHA a0a7c2c994ab: 7 checks all green before, 8 checks with `manifest` red after, and reinstalling the previous copy restored the green. There is no single-file remedy, because SHOP-INVARIANTS.json is gitignored and make_invariants.py derives it from `git ls-files` at ONE commit, so a hand-edited hash would only make the manifest lie about which commit it represents. This entry therefore deploys as part of a full tree sync that regenerates the manifest at the same commit. Being caught is the property the entry was added for, so a red here is the check working rather than a reason to loosen it.

The WhatsApp start gate, and the entry that brings it under drift detection at all. The copy that has been running lives at ~/whatsapp_posture_guard.sh -- OUTSIDE ZEROCLAW_HOME, which is the root every dst here resolves against, so no entry could reach it and nothing hashed it. That left two copies of one safety check, this repo's tracked scripts/whatsapp_posture_guard.sh and the box's, never compared against each other: the same two-copies shape this file already documents for pay_link.py, on a script whose whole job is refusing a fail-open config. Placing it at bin/ puts its hash in the manifest, so an edit to the deployed guard now reports as drift. EXPECT THIS TO READ MISSING ON THE FIRST RUN, because nothing has ever placed a file at that path; per the note above, a dst nobody has confirmed failing loud is the safe direction and the first run is how it gets confirmed. Scoped to the one filename because scripts/ also tracks test_whatsapp_posture_guard.sh, which is a CI control and has no business on the box. DO NOT DEPLOY THIS WITHOUT DIFFING THE TWO COPIES FIRST: a sync overwrites the box copy with this one, and if they differ, the difference is a finding to read rather than a file to clobber.

The confirmer the announcer shells out to, and the thing that actually derives every announced field from the chain rather than from model prose. announce_settlements.sh resolves it at $ZC_TOOLS/confirm_settlements.py and exits 2 without it, so its absence degrades the deterministic path to a no-op that still exits non-zero. Scoped to the one filename because demo/ also tracks test_confirm_settlements.py, which has no business in a jailed agent workspace.

_units_doc: SHOULD THE UNIT FILES THEMSELVES COME UNDER THE DRIFT GATE? Decided 2026-08-27, after a
grep of the bare zc-shop.service file read ZERO ExecStartPre lines against a merged unit
that carries one from a drop-in. The answer is YES at the DIRECTIVE level and NO at the
distinction is the whole decision rather than a hedge.
THE CASE FOR BYTE-LEVEL GATING, which is the obvious move and is what `map` already does
for every other artifact. A unit file is executable configuration on a box that takes
money; an edit to zc-shop.service is at least as consequential as an edit to a skill, and
skills are hashed. zc-qr.service and zc-tunnel.service are not even NAMED anywhere in this
file, so nothing notices if either changes or disappears, and nothing asserts that
zc-shop's own ExecStartPre is still there.
WHY IT IS REFUSED ANYWAY, on two grounds that are mechanical rather than aesthetic.
FIRST, THE SCHEMA CANNOT EXPRESS IT. Every `dst` here resolves against ZEROCLAW_HOME.
Units live in ~/.config/systemd/user, which is not under that root, so a unit entry in
`map` is not merely unconventional, it has nowhere to point.
SECOND, AND THE REASON THAT WOULD SURVIVE FIXING THE FIRST: a byte comparison needs a
tracked copy to compare against, and no tracked copy of zc-shop.service exists. Writing
one from inference and hashing it would make the manifest assert a fiction, and the
manifest is the artifact whose whole value is that it does not. The consequence is already
measured in this repo: deploy/x402-feed-gate.service was committed as a proposal with an
ExecStart pointing at a binary that does not exist, and installing it verbatim would have
failed 203/EXEC on every start. A guessed unit is worse than no unit, because someone will
eventually cp it. It would also be red forever until someone reconciled it, and this file
already records what a permanent red does: `a red that never changes reads as a known
issue`, which is how the mint scan sat broken while reporting.
WHAT SHIPS INSTEAD: `require_directives` above, asserted by box_selfcheck against the
definition it ALREADY collects from `systemctl cat`. It needs no tracked unit file, it
cannot assert a fiction because it only ever states a positive requirement, it survives a
unit being legitimately reorganised, and it goes red on the one thing that matters. It also
reaches drop-ins for free, since `systemctl cat` merges them.
AND THE GUARD SCRIPT ITSELF IS NOW BYTE-GATED, which is the half that was genuinely
missing. Its `map` entry above hashes it. So the split is: the SCRIPT is content and gets a
hash; the UNIT is a declaration and gets an assertion.
zc-qr.service AND zc-tunnel.service ARE DELIBERATELY STILL ABSENT FROM `units`. Adding
them is one line each and it was not done, because `units` means MUST BE ALIVE and neither
has been observed. If zc-qr is a oneshot that ran once to link a session, listing it
manufactures a permanent red on a healthy box, which is the failure this file already warns
about twice. The honest sequence is to read their type and state off the box first, then
add them with the verdict their type deserves. Until then their absence is a KNOWN gap
stated here rather than an oversight, and it is the one thing on this list still owed.

units.why: The agent daemon. Nothing else on this list matters if it is down.
units.why_require_directives: WHAT THIS ROW ASSERTS AND WHY NOTHING ELSE DOES. zc-shop.service takes its ExecStartPre from a systemd drop-in at ~/.config/systemd/user/zc-shop.service.d/10-posture-guard.conf, so grepping the bare unit file reads ZERO in both the wired and the unwired world and cannot answer the question; `systemctl --user cat` merges drop-ins and is the surface that can. Read that way on 2026-08-27 the box reports ExecStartPre 1 and ExecStart 1. The liveness row above cannot see this either -- a shop with no pre-check running is ACTIVE, so it is green -- and check_unit_definitions already COLLECTS the merged definition and only PUBLISHES it, so the directive has been sitting in the /selfcheck payload with nothing reading the value back. This field is the assertion, and it is what makes losing the guard loud. The value is a SUBSTRING matched against the joined directive values rather than a full path, so relocating the script or adding arguments does not turn it red while deleting the drop-in does. Pulling deploy/zc-shop.service.d/ under pressure is the correct move at the wrong moment, and this ensures the next hourly selfcheck says so out loud instead of the guard quietly staying gone.

units.why: Schedules the DePIN feed publisher. A stopped timer is the death of the submission's most defensible claim, and it used to PASS this gate.
The oneshot the timer drives. Healthy when inactive with Result=success; a crash is inactive too, which is why Result rather than ActiveState decides it.
The machine paywall. Answers HTTP 402 and is the surface a judge can exercise.
units.template_status: UNVERIFIED against the box, same convention as an unconfirmed dst. The unit installed on the node was never read from here -- every remote-hands route into it is currently shut -- so the file is a proposal for what it should be rather than a record of what it is. box_selfcheck.py now publishes each unit's definition (structure only, no values) into the /selfcheck verdict; reconcile every UNVERIFIED line in the template against that payload on the first fetch after the deploy freeze lifts.

units.why: The Cloudflare tunnel that makes the gate reachable. The gate being alive behind a dead tunnel looks identical to the gate being down.

Schedules the deterministic settlement announcer. Listed here because a replacement nobody schedules does not replace anything: the prose SOP it supersedes is still installable, and the only thing separating the two is which one a timer drives. Expect this to read MISSING on its first run if the unit was never installed, which is the point -- an absent timer is currently indistinguishable from a running one, and that is exactly the state in which a fabricated confirmation would reach a customer.

mint_scan_extra.why: The 2026-08-06 incident surface: the skill on disk was already correct while three brain.db rows still held the devnet mint, so a file-to-file comparison could never have seen it. THE PATH WAS WRONG UNTIL 2026-08-16 and this entry scanned nothing: it read agents/demo/workspace/memory/, a directory that does not exist on the box, while the live database is at data/memory/brain.db (245,760 B, with -wal and -shm siblings, and a brain.db.bak-premint dated the morning of that same incident). The check failed MISSING rather than passing, which is the honest direction, and it is also why nobody chased it: a red that never changes reads as a known issue.
mint_scan_extra.why_denylist: Once the path was corrected the scan ran for the first time and MEASURED the noise premise the previous note only suspected: 27 distinct unexpected base58 tokens, each appearing exactly ONCE in real content, all of them one-off Solana Pay reference keys. (The probe's 54 occurrences are memories_fts mirroring memories; box_selfcheck reads bytes and dedupes per file, so the index mirror was never the noise.) An allowlist over agent memory is unbounded BY CONSTRUCTION, because a reference key is a fresh random address per order and the legitimate set grows with every sale. So the polarity is inverted here and only here: this target is scanned for KNOWN-RETIRED mints, which is what a check named mint-prohibition should always have meant, and which is finite and auditable. The 2026-08-06 mint is retired, so the incident is still caught; box_selfcheck --self-test drives both directions against a synthetic brain.db with this table shape. Do NOT fix future noise by populating known_other with observed tokens: that would bless the current state including drift. The two honest levers are retiring an address in retired_mints_extra, or disabling this entry WITH the reason.

_retired_mints_extra_doc: Extra addresses the state scan must treat as prohibited, beyond the ones already derived.
The generator derives the base list from its MINT_NETWORK table minus the configured mint,
so the devnet USDC mint is prohibited without being listed here. This is for an address
that was never in that table: a rotated merchant wallet, a mint from a superseded
Entries are validated as base58 and refused if they name the configured mint, because a
typo here is a prohibition that matches nothing and reports clean forever. Like
allowed_addresses, it is never auto-populated: a denylist harvested from the box would
inherit exactly the failure mode of the allowlist it replaced.
_allowed_addresses_doc: Base58 addresses that may legitimately appear in a deployed file besides the merchant and
the mint. Measured 2026-08-06 across every tracked file under skills/ and sops/: the only
foreign tokens anywhere are two fixtures inside test_pay_link.py, and test files are
excluded from the scan by rule, so this list is correctly empty.
It is NOT auto-populated, and that is the design decision. A generator that allowlisted
whatever it found would bless the current state, including drift, which is the one thing
this manifest exists to detect. A new address here is a deliberate declaration.
_known_other_doc: Consumed by box_selfcheck's ALLOWLIST scan over deployed files as a second suppression
list. Empty on purpose, and it should stay that way: the allowlist now covers only files
this repo writes and hashes, where measurement found no foreign tokens at all, so a
suppression there would be hiding real drift rather than real noise. It no longer applies
to brain.db, which is scanned with the opposite polarity.
